sectors.name: Core
sectors.description: Reusable software foundations: kernel contracts, data access, messaging, web integration, secrets and shared accounts.
sectors.overview: Core groups the libraries and account foundations used across studio software. Published packages coexist with work still in development; consult each project for its supported capabilities and release status.
sectors.philosophy: Truth is structure. Beauty is predictability. The Core holds both without apology.

sectors.name: Ops
sectors.description: Build workflows, infrastructure and operational tooling for developing and maintaining studio software.
sectors.overview: Ops brings together reusable build workflows and operational projects. HoneyDrunk.Actions owns current shared CI workflows; the older Pipelines project is deprecated. Catalog concepts do not imply deployed automation or a hosted service.
sectors.philosophy: Automation is faith made mechanical. Trust the ritual, and the Hive moves.

sectors.name: HoneyNet
sectors.description: Security-related software and research concepts, including proposed defensive tools and authorized testing environments.
sectors.overview: HoneyNet groups security-oriented concepts in the Grid. BreachLab and Sentinel remain Seed projects. This sector does not advertise a live security platform, a testing service or completed product integrations.
sectors.philosophy: Security isn't silence — it's the sound of systems learning to heal.

sectors.name: Creator
sectors.description: Creative tooling concepts for working with assets, narrative and publishing alongside the studio’s own visual development.
sectors.overview: Creator maps ideas for tools supporting creative work. Its catalog includes early concepts, rather than an available campaign, analytics or asset-marketplace platform. Current visual development contributes directly to the studio’s games and shared universe.
sectors.philosophy: Every signal starts as an idea. Creator turns it into resonance.

sectors.name: Market
sectors.description: Apps that bring studio ideas into everyday use, led by Pocket Quests, an illustrated quest journal in development.
sectors.overview: Market is the app side of the studio. Pocket Quests is in active development, with planning, quests, progress and place discovery. Other Seed entries are future concepts, not finished apps or public SaaS offerings. A catalog listing is not a launch, pricing or revenue claim.
sectors.philosophy: Build useful things. Let real use shape what comes next.

sectors.name: HoneyPlay
sectors.description: Original games and a shared fantasy universe: Magic Shop development, elemental lore, creatures and visual exploration.
sectors.overview: HoneyPlay brings together original games and the setting behind them. Magic Shop combines shopkeeping, crafting and a guild hall of returning adventurers. Shared-universe work develops elemental powers, peoples, creatures and visual references. The separate Seat Game card-battler prototype is paused. Games have their own implementations; shared lore does not imply shared runtime-service integration or a public release.
sectors.philosophy: Play reveals the truth of the system. Emotion is the final debug.

sectors.name: Cyberware
sectors.description: A future-facing catalog of robotics, simulation and hardware-interface concepts.
sectors.overview: Cyberware preserves proposed robotics and simulation directions. Its current entries are Seed concepts, not delivered hardware products or a working simulation-to-robotics platform. This sector is a map of possibilities rather than an active product announcement.
sectors.philosophy: Structure meets soul. Code meets art. In Cyberware, it also meets gravity.

sectors.name: Meta
sectors.description: Studio documentation, code standards and the website that maps projects and their public updates.
sectors.overview: Meta holds the studio’s planning, documentation and shared engineering standards. HoneyDrunk.Documentation owns product and architecture decisions; this website publishes bounded, dated summaries. HoneyHub remains archived. Proposed portals and knowledge tools are catalog concepts, not available hosted products.
sectors.philosophy: Understanding is the only form of immortality the Hive allows.
sectors.tagline: Know the map. Tend the garden.

sectors.name: AI
sectors.description: AI libraries and agent-tooling concepts, alongside practical AI assistance in studio engineering and creative work.
sectors.overview: AI groups the Grid’s library and agent-tooling projects. Published software and provider support must be checked at the individual project or package level; the catalog does not establish an operating autonomous agent network. AI assists the studio’s engineering, documentation and visual exploration under human direction and review.
sectors.philosophy: Intelligence is not awareness — it's alignment, remembered in code.
